text:
alex: Quick heads-up — found a reproducible throughput drop when we push max_tokens_per_batch above ~2k on A10s. Profiling suggests KV-fragmentation triggers a kernel fallback that increases latency and reduces packing efficiency.

maria: Oof. Is this specific to a model shape or sequence length distribution?

alex: Seems worst with mix-heavy tails: many short requests + occasional long completions. A10 kernel selector falls back to a conservative path when KV frag > ~12% (we saw ~18%). H100/A100 less affected but still noticeable at extreme batch sizes.

lee: Can you paste the profiler snippet?

alex: Sure — here's the critical bit:

```
# profiler excerpt (aggregated)
model: llama-13b
cards: A10
max_tokens_per_batch=4096 -> throughput -22%
kv_frag_ratio: 0.18
kernel: fallback_conv2 -> +1.9x per-token latency
batch_pack_efficiency: 0.71 -> 0.58
```

maria: Hmm. That explains the hit. So two knobs: reduce max_tokens_per_batch on A10, or change queue policy to gate long tails so they don't fragment hot slices.

jas: What if we keep max_batch_size high but cap max_tokens_per_batch lower for A10/T4/L4 and allow higher for A100/H100? Mixed cards should apply card-class overrides.

lee: Agreed. Proposed quick policy:
- A10/T4/L4: max_tokens_per_batch = 2048, max_batch_size = 64
- A100/H100: max_tokens_per_batch = 8192, max_batch_size = 128
- KV_FRAG_THRESHOLD: 0.12 (trigger queue rebalancing)

alex: I like that. Also change kernel_selector to prefer 'kv-friendly' kernels for mixed packing: `kernel_selector: dynamic_pref_kv` so we bias to kernels that tolerate fragmentation.

maria: We should be careful with perf regressions on H100 when forcing kv-friendly kernels. Can we A/B by route (canary on 5% traffic)?

jas: Plan for canary: implement card-class overrides + kv_frag threshold + kernel_selector flag. Metrics to track: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, batch_pack_efficiency, kernel_fallback_count, kv_frag_ratio. Rollback if p95 increases >5% or tokens/sec drops >7%.

ci-bot: test-run started for PR #4521 — e2e microbench with mixed tails (100k reqs) on staging-cluster.

lee: Nice. Also add a small synthetic that pushes many short requests back-to-back to provoke fragmentation. We need worst-case safety checks.

alex: I'll draft the config change and test harness. Jasper, can you own the canary dashboard? Need token-level cost too.

jas: On it. I'll sketch the dashboard and set alert thresholds.

maria: One more thought: consider prefetch-aware packing — if we detect long KV chains about to be read, we can gate their admission until a warm slot opens. Might reduce fragmentation without changing user-facing caps. Worth an experiment later.

alex: Agree — follow-up. For now implement card-class max_tokens adjustments + kv_frag threshold + kernel bias. I'll open the PR and link benchmarks.

ci-bot: PR #4521 status: tests passed (unit), perf-run queued.

lee: Thanks — if perf-run looks good, let's ship to 5% canary tomorrow morning. :rocket:

alex: 👍 will post results here as soon as CI perf-run completes.
